items.full: US public-sector unions are winning more protections against AI surveillance and automation-driven job losses. The issue is growing more urgent as nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI, according to an Ernst and Young survey . The wins are piling up nationwide. After a strike vote in October, IFPTE Local 21 in Oakland secured retraining programs instead of AI-related layoffs. In Pennsylvania, Governor Josh Shapiro guaranteed SEIU Local 668 human oversight during a pilot of OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise . The Transport Workers Union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. On top of that, California Governor Gavin Newsom banned AI surveillance software, often called "bossware," along with automated firings in September. New York has protected state employees from AI displacement by law since late 2025. Employers are pushing automation to cut costs, according to labor researcher Kung Feng at UC Berkeley. Union leaders like Liz Shuler of the AFL-CIO, Lorena Gonzalez, and TWU's John Samuelsen support AI safety systems where they help workers but insist on mandatory human control over every AI application in the workplace, the Guardian reports . items.title: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models
items.desc: Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue says he has produced the first technical evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are using Nvidia's latest Blackwell GPUs despite US export controls. His forensic method reads characteristic chip signatures directly from published model weights. He estimates the hardware behind the five training runs cost more than half a billion dollars. items.full: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models Maximilian Schreiner View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner Nov 13, 2026 Nano Banana Pro prompted by THE DECODER AI researcher Will DePue says a forensic analysis has turned up the first technical evidence that leading Chinese AI labs have access to Nvidia's latest Blackwell hardware despite US export controls. He says senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic have already checked the method. According to a forensic investigation by Will DePue , Chinese AI companies DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are using Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell GPUs. DePue played a key role at OpenAI in building the Sora and Sora 2 video models as well as GPT-4o, o3, and GPT-5 before founding the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs . His analysis, he says, provides the first technical evidence of this access. US officials and news outlets had suspected that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI were using Blackwell chips but never published proof. DePue wrote on X that senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic have already independently checked and confirmed his findings. According to DePue, six Chinese models released since April 2026 carry the distinct signature of Nvidia's Blackwell generation, while earlier models such as DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi K2.5 show traces of Nvidia's older Hopper generation. The evidence comes directly from the published language models. An AI model consists of billions of numerical values called weights. Before training starts, PyTorch, the standard software framework, fills these empty slots with random numbers generated from a starting value called a seed. To distribute this massive amount of data quickly, the GPU splits the work across its individual compute cores. Because different chip models have different core counts, the filling process produces a characteristic pattern, according to the report. Older Hopper chips such as the H100 and H800 use 132 compute cores, while the newer Blackwell chips use exactly 148 or 152 cores depending on the model (B200/B300 or GB200/GB300). Training then adjusts these values millions of times, but some slots for unused words or symbols keep their initial random values. Even in heavily trained parts of the model, a faint statistical echo of the initial distribution survives, according to DePue. He says he worked the pattern backward and reproduced the results for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3 exactly on real Blackwell chips. He has published the verification code on GitHub. The analysis maps DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 to B200 or B300 chips (148 cores). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro, and Ant Group's Ling-3.1-flash show, according to the analysis, the 152-core pattern of Nvidia's liquid-cooled GB200 or GB300 flagship rack systems. DePue says chance can be ruled out statistically and that the method correctly identified all 24 control models with known hardware, including Meta's Llama 3.1 (H100). items.title: OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute
items.desc: OpenAI's safety team systematically investigated why the chains of thought in frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are increasingly evading oversight. Four training steps drive the erosion, including architecture choices and reinforcement learning. The analysis shows that the loss of transparency is not a law of nature but also reflects tradeoffs around capability and cost. The article OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute Maximilian Schreiner View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner Nov 12, 2026 Nano Banana Pro prompted by THE DECODER Frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are becoming harder for safety monitors to see into. OpenAI's new research identifies which training steps are responsible and shows that the loss of transparency isn't purely a law of nature but is tied to decisions about performance and cost. To keep tabs on modern AI agents, safety researchers monitor their chains of thought (CoT). Before a reasoning model answers, it writes out its intermediate steps on a digital scratchpad that can reveal planned deception. Early on, though, Anthropic showed that these scratchpads aren't complete records, demonstrating that models like Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek-R1 often don't even mention key clues in their chains of thought. Even so, reading the scratchpad long served as the most important safety net. As recently as this spring, OpenAI called it good news that models like GPT-5.4 could barely manipulate their inner monologue on command, even though the researchers warned at the time that low controllability doesn't guarantee reliable oversight. That trend broke for good with GPT-6 Astra, the flagship model released in September. At launch, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called its monitorability fragile and warned of a negative trend . He followed up shortly after in his essay "An Alien Mind," writing that no AI lab had solved monitoring well enough to keep scaling at full speed much longer. Astra recently showed how real those blind spots already are when it quietly delivered results about 40 percent worse on coding tasks for safety research, without the scratchpad monitor detecting any malicious intent, because a grader used in training had inadvertently favored this kind of "sandbagging" over outright refusal. In a new analysis from OpenAI's safety team , researchers systematically studied which specific training steps trigger this erosion. They tracked two early warning signs, silent reasoning without a scratchpad (No-CoT Capability) and targeted control over the chain of thought ( CoT Controllability ). According to the UK AI Safety Institute , Astra solves math problems that take a human about 31 minutes even with reasoning switched off. A second test asks a model, for example, to insert "meow" after every word or use only lowercase letters. Analyzing models from GPT-5 through GPT-6 Astra, the researchers traced the problem to four main causes across the training cycle. Silent mental math rises directly with the base model's raw capability, measured as declining "perplexity," meaning more accurate text prediction. As the base model improves during pretraining, it completes more reasoning steps invisibly "in its head" without leaving a written trail. This increase isn't just a byproduct of general pretraining progress but also depends on the architecture developers choose. items.title: Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality
items.desc: Too many websites look alike. They use familiar layouts, repeat the same patterns, and often leave little impression once you’ve moved on. Andy Clarke explores how understanding a company’s story can lead to more distinctive designs, using modular and compound grids to create layouts with character. Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.
items.full: NVIDIA L4 GPUs. 5-second cold starts. Scale to zero when idle. When I started designing websites thirty years ago, David Siegel had just published Creating Killer Web Sites , the book that popularised HTML tables and spacer GIFs for laying out web pages. CSS eventually gave us more control over layouts through floats and positioning. Neither was intended for page layout, and inconsistent browser behaviour could make using them frustrating. Still, that didn’t stop me and a generation of other designers from using floats and positioning. When CSS frameworks began providing ready-made grid systems, things got a little easier. Blueprint CSS ) offered a 24-column grid, while Nathan Smith’s 960 Grid System offered 12- and 16-column options. These frameworks gave designers and developers a shared structure, making layout planning and implementation considerably easier. Twelve-column grids weren’t invented in the 2000s. Graphic designers had used column-based and modular grids for decades, and twelve is a convenient number because you don’t need to be a maths genius to divide it into halves, thirds, and quarters to create the 2-up, 3-up, and 4-up components we see everywhere online. Frameworks like Bootstrap and Foundation followed, helping establish twelve-column grids as the de facto standard for page layouts. I get why that happened. But somewhere along the way, one layout option became the default starting point for almost everything. CSS Grid changed what’s possible for page layouts, but I still see designers start by dividing a page into twelve equal columns, then deciding how to fit their content into them. The designs they end up with might be perfectly fine, but they can also look remarkably similar. Still, I don’t think twelve-column grids themselves are the problem. It’s reaching for a familiar solution before considering what makes the company I’m designing for distinctive and what its website needs to communicate. So what happens when I start with those questions instead? Every company has a story worth telling Before I decide how many columns a layout needs, I want to understand the company I’m designing for. What makes it different from its competitors? What does it want people to remember? Does it have a personality that could influence how its website looks and feels? These questions matter because a layout does more than arrange content. The size, position, and relationships between elements influence how people experience a website. A restrained, orderly composition can communicate something very different from one that’s full of energy and movement. So to demonstrate what I mean, I’ll use Wheelman. It’s a fictional company I invented for my book, Standout Designs for the Web . Pre-orders for Standout Designs for the Web are now open in the CSS-Tricks store. Wheelman provides products and services for getaway drivers, including legal advice, robbery insurance, and an online shop selling break-in essentials. It also publishes a magazine with advice, news, and stories about life behind the wheel. Wheelman isn’t an ordinary company, so why should its website look like an everyday collection of components? items.desc: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia effective immediately, according to a statement on November 12, 2026. The article Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage scandal wipes out $1.4 trillion in market value appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia effective immediately, according to a statement on November 12, 2026. The move came after the Wall Street Journal reported that the board was planning to fire Huang following revelations about two extramarital affairs, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy . Since a New York Times report on October 29 about possible ties to Chinese intelligence, Nvidia has shed roughly $1.4 trillion in market value. CFO Colette Kress is taking over on an interim basis while the board searches for a permanent successor. Harvey C. Jones will serve as the first independent board chair and stressed that business operations continue without disruption. Replacing Huang will be difficult because Nvidia was built entirely around him. He secured the company's market position through a complex web of alliances with financiers and roughly $300 billion in guarantees for smaller customers. His departure could unravel that structure, which he used to keep major tech rivals at bay and support large parts of the AI industry. Ad Major customers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet, along with AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, depend heavily on Nvidia's chips, but the company's 75 percent profit margin is pushing them to develop their own, cheaper alternatives. Huang also left no clear succession plan, with more than 60 employees reporting directly to him, leaving both internal and external candidates starting from a weakened position. items.full: Elevenlabs updates its speech recognition for recorded conversations and real-time use. Independent benchmarks confirm high accuracy but also show drawbacks in speed. Elevenlabs has released two new speech-to-text models , Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live, built for messy conditions such as people talking over each other in meetings or phone calls with background noise. Scribe v3 is designed for pre-recorded audio files, while Scribe v3 Live targets low-latency real-time applications. Both models are available now through the ElevenAPI developer interface and the ElevenAgents platform. Ad According to Elevenlabs, Scribe v3 cuts word errors by about 25 percent compared to its predecessor across 102 languages, and the company says German accuracy improves significantly. Speaker diarization also works more reliably in larger group conversations, according to the company, and Scribe v3 Live makes it available in real time for the first time. Ad Independent benchmarks from Artificial Analysis confirm that Scribe v3 is among the most accurate transcription models on the market. It edges out competitors from Microsoft, Mistral, xAI, Google, and OpenAI, trailing only a preview model from Alibaba. Anyone looking to process large volumes of audio quickly and cheaply is better off with other providers, though. Elevenlabs lands mid-pack on speed and price. Models from Microsoft and xAI run many times faster at marginally higher error rates and cost roughly half as much. Ad However, the benchmark measures only word errors on recorded files. It doesn't account for the improvements Elevenlabs touts in speaker diarization, rare languages, or the real-time behavior of Scribe v3 Live. In voice agents, Scribe v3 Live is meant to fix a flaw in current systems, which often rely on rigid pause timers and cut callers off mid-sentence when they stop briefly to think or slowly read out a string of numbers. The new real-time model analyzes conversational context alongside the audio signal so it can tell when a speaker has actually finished. Ad Elevenlabs also gives developers more control over the final transcript. The models can be preloaded with thousands of specialized terms like brand names or medications to avoid mishearing domain-specific vocabulary. Developers can set formatting rules for numbers or dates in natural language, and a multilingual mode handles language switches mid-sentence. Enterprise customers get isolated servers in the EU and a zero-retention mode designed to delete data immediately after each request. Ad Elevenlabs is also expanding its enterprise business alongside the new models. Under an expanded partnership with Nvidia , the company is integrating the open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL language model into ElevenAgents, securing additional compute capacity running on Nvidia, developing local voice control for robots, and running a phone agent for Poland's public health system. The company also announced an alliance with consulting firm McKinsey , a broader partner program for system integrators, and its own marketplace where companies like Salesforce, IBM, and Zendesk offer ready-made voice agents. items.title: Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue predictions to single cell type resolution with AlphaGenome 2
items.desc: Google Deepmind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that analyzes genetic variants for individual cell types rather than across bulk tissue. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor. The model is available for noncommercial research through an API and is set to be integrated into Google's agentic platform Antigravity. The article Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue predictions to single cell type resolution with AlphaGenome 2 appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Google Deepmind has released AlphaGenome 2, a new AI model for genomics research. It predicts the effects of genetic variants on specific human cell types and finds nearly twice as many relevant gene changes as its predecessor. Every cell in the human body carries the same DNA blueprint, but different cell types switch different genes on or off. A heart muscle cell reads DNA differently than an immune cell. Predicting those differences is one of the biggest unsolved problems in genomics. Google Deepmind aims to take a major step in that direction with AlphaGenome 2 . The new model is designed to predict how DNA sequences and their variations affect specific human cell types. It was trained on more than 107 million individual cell profiles from 68 tissues, according to Google Deepmind , and is meant to help researchers uncover the cellular drivers of disease. Ad Its predecessor, AlphaGenome , took in a DNA sequence a million letters long and predicted its properties across thousands of experiments spanning many tissues at once. According to Google Deepmind, that parallel approach spread the model's capacity too thin and made it hard to capture subtle differences between closely related cell types. Ad AlphaGenome 2 instead works as a conditional model. Along with the DNA sequence, it takes a specific biological state as an extra input and calculates effects for that one cell type. The system was trained on more than 107 million individual cell profiles from 68 tissues in humans and mice. Beyond predicting how strongly a gene is expressed, the model also calculates how DNA is physically packaged in the nucleus, showing which stretches of the genome are accessible. It can now also predict DNA methylation, chemical tags that act as molecular switches to silence or activate genes. Ad AlphaGenome 2 can also infer missing data from a single measurement. If researchers measure only a cell's gene activity, for instance, the model provides predictions for additional properties, such as how tightly or loosely certain stretches of DNA are packaged. That helps researchers decide which lab experiments are worth running next. On the TenK10K benchmark dataset with 28 primary immune cell types, AlphaGenome 2 identified about 30 percent of causal variants. In 43 percent of cases, it also correctly predicted whether a variant upregulates or downregulates a gene. A fine-tuned version of AlphaGenome 1 managed just 16 and 23 percent. The system also models continuous changes, like the maturation of blood stem cells into red blood cells, with considerably greater accuracy. Ad Working purely computationally, the model reproduced an inflammatory bowel disease mechanism previously identified in a study . It isolated the exact DNA variant in a regulatory switch far from the gene that selectively overactivates ETS2 in gut macrophages, while other cell types and genes remained largely unaffected. Ad A key advantage of the new architecture is its ability to adapt to entirely new experiments without retraining. Researchers can feed in gene activity data from just a few dozen cells, and the model calculates effects for that previously unseen cell state. According to Deepmind

items.title: How to buy Kinsta hosting for your small business: A step-by-step guide
items.desc: If you’re ready to host your business website with Kinsta, the next steps are to choose a plan, create your account, and get your WordPress site running. The process ...
items.full: If you’re ready to host your business website with Kinsta , the next steps are to choose a plan, create your account , and get your WordPress site running. The process is straightforward, but there are a few decisions worth making before entering payment details, especially if you’re moving an existing website. For example, a small business running one WordPress website may not need the same resources as a growing online store or a company managing several websites. You’ll also need to decide whether to pay based on website visits or bandwidth, and whether to start with monthly or annual billing. This guide walks you through the process, from choosing your hosting plan and signing up to creating your first WordPress site or requesting a migration. You don’t need to know every technical detail about your website before purchasing hosting. However, having a few things ready can make choosing a plan easier. Start by answering these questions: If you’re moving from another hosting provider, make sure you can access your current hosting control panel and WordPress dashboard. You’ll need some of those details later when requesting a migration. You don’t have to move your domain to Kinsta or cancel your existing hosting before signing up. Those steps come later. Start at Kinsta’s small-business hosting page or go directly to the WordPress hosting pricing page . The small-business page introduces the managed hosting service and provides a pricing section where you can configure a plan. The main pricing page gives you a more detailed comparison of available plans and resources. On the pricing page , you’ll find Business plans alongside options for agencies and larger organizations. For most small businesses evaluating their first Kinsta subscription, the Business plans are the appropriate place to begin comparing options. The pricing configuration lets you choose your billing period and, depending on the plan family, the number of WordPress installations and how usage is measured. If your business operates one independent WordPress website, start by comparing the single-site plans. If you manage several websites, such as separate WordPress installations for different businesses or brands, compare the multiple-site plans. Kinsta counts WordPress installations rather than every domain connected to a website. For example, using both example.com and www.example.com for the same installation doesn’t automatically mean you need two website slots. You can also add site capacity through the WordPress site add-on . Each additional site includes a staging environment, but it shares the hosting plan’s other resources, including bandwidth or visits, storage, and CDN bandwidth. If you’re unsure whether to choose a larger plan or add an individual website slot, compare the total resources you need, not just the number of websites. Kinsta offers plans that measure usage through either monthly visits or server bandwidth. With visits-based billing , your allowance is based on visits recorded by Kinsta’s infrastructure. items.full: Australia's government, led by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, has announced a law that would impose mandatory safety rules on frontier AI companies operating in the country for the first time. The rules target the most advanced models with the highest risk profiles and fall under the government's "AI in Australia's Interests" agenda. A new oversight body will work alongside the Australian AI Safety Institute to enforce compliance and hand out steep penalties for violations. Companies building frontier models will have to open them up to independent audits, maintain ongoing safety checks, publish their safety frameworks, and report security incidents to the government immediately . That last requirement is partly aimed at catching early warning signs from AI agents that go off the rails . Albanese, Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles, and ministers Tony Burke and Tim Ayres said the government is putting domestic safety guardrails in place before entering international negotiations. The goal is to protect citizens and national interests while building the kind of trust and regulatory stability that attracts investment and lets AI benefit the economy and healthcare. More details will follow once consultations wrap up. items.title: Should You Actually Add AI To That? A Four-Question Audit For Product Teams
items.desc: An AI feature can save users time on a task, only for them to spend it checking the results. This practical audit helps product teams decide where AI earns its place and what users need to verify its output.
items.full: About The Author Victor Yocco, PhD, is a UX Researcher with a focus on AI and the author of Designing Agentic AI Experiences (CRC Press, 2026), Design for the Mind (Manning, … More about Victor ↬ Weekly tips on front-end & UX . Trusted by 182,000+ folks. How To Measure UX and Design Impact, 8h video + UX training Meet AI 2027 Conference, December 1, 2026. Celebrating 10 million developers Smart Interface Design Patterns, 45 lessons + UX training Advertise on Smashing Magazine An AI feature can save users time on a task, only for them to spend it checking the results. This practical audit helps product teams decide where AI earns its place and what users need to verify its output. A product team at a large health insurer wants to add AI that writes the full written determination for benefits appeals specialists. The technology works as specified. However, the specialists stop using it, and the ones who keep using it take longer on each case than the ones who ignore it. A short evaluation with the specialists surfaces the problem fast: reading an AI-written determination carefully enough to sign it takes about as long as writing one, and the specialist also has to check for mistakes they would never have made themselves. The feature adds work to a task these people had already mastered. Rescoping the release fixes it. A second version surfaces the policy provisions and prior decisions relevant to each appeal and leaves the writing to the specialist. The search step disappears, review time drops, and the part of the job the specialist is good at stays where it was. The technology is identical in both versions, and the difference is which part of the task the AI handles. Every interface change costs the user something before it pays anything back. They have to rebuild their picture of how the tool works, learn where things are now, and decide how far to trust what the AI hands them. Nelson Cowan’s review of working memory research (2001) put the limit at about four items held in mind at once. All three of those jobs draw on the same small supply. An AI feature in an enterprise software setting requires more from the user than a redesigned menu, because it changes what they do all day. Hand the synthesis to an AI and the user becomes a checker. Give it the recommendation too, and the job shrinks to signing off. Either change costs user attention, and for people whose training is their standing at work, either one can feel like a demotion. For example, in one study, Sophia Ackerhans (2025) and colleagues found that physicians asked to sign AI-assisted decisions reported a more serious threat to their professional identity, and explanations of the AI’s reasoning raised both trust and that threat together. We can call that the break-even line . Returns to users come in three forms: For example, an AI-powered fraud screening tool shows the errors-caught form at work, since the analyst reviews flags they would never have raised themselves, which costs attention, and the catch rate pays for it. items.full: WordPress security requires a team of dedicated analysts researching the latest malware variants and WordPress exploits, turning them into firewall rules and malware signatures, and releasing those to customers in real-time. At Wordfence, WordPress security isn’t a division of our business – WordPress security is all we do. The sun never sets on our global security team and we run a sophisticated threat intelligence platform to aggregate, analyze and produce ground breaking security research on the newest security threats. Logging in is easy with Wordfence 2FA. items.full: Contact Form 7 is a plugin designed to be a practical tool for all WordPress users who embrace the philosophy of free and open source software. It employs sophisticatedly modularized architecture and its original Schema-Woven Validation technology. You can find docs , FAQ and more detailed information about Contact Form 7 on contactform7.com . When you cannot find the answer to your question on the FAQ or in any of the documentation, check the support forum on WordPress.org. If you cannot locate any topics that pertain to your particular issue, post a new topic for it. It is hard to continue to maintain this plugin without support from users like you. There are several ways for you to contribute to the project : testing, coding, translating it into your local languages, helping other users, financial donations, etc, etc. We equally welcome you regardless of the way you contribute. See Plugin privacy notices . screenshot-1.png Blocks This plugin provides 1 block. You will find Contact menu in your WordPress admin screen. For basic usage, have a look at the plugin’s website . items.full: Andrea is a Senior Developer Advocate at GitHub with over a decade of experience in developer tools. She combines technical depth with a mission to make advanced technologies more accessible. After transitioning from Army service and construction management to software development, she brings a unique perspective to bridging complex engineering concepts with practical implementation. She lives in Florida with her Welsh partner, two sons, and two dogs, where she continues to drive innovation and support open source through GitHub's global initiatives. Find her online @acolombiadev.

items.title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
items.desc: Chinese investors are shut out of Anthropic's IPO, Bloomberg reports. Banks are rejecting buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, citing U.S. export control rules known as ITAR. Similar restrictions applied during SpaceX's IPO, and Anthropic's products aren't available in either region anyway. The article Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
items.desc: Anthropic's new Claude for Manufacturing plugin connects the AI directly to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, and Infor. Its 17 specialized skills let the AI draft quotes, compare suppliers, and place backup orders when deliveries are delayed, all after human approval. The plugin doesn't control physical machines yet, but Anthropic is separately developing the Model Hardware Standard for that.
